The components

Source: vignettes/articles/components.Rmd
components.Rmd

Each component answers a question people ask when they look at a map. The examples use jp_prefectures, five prefectures of Japan from north to south, and earthquakes, points in southern South America.

library(mapgl)
library(maplore)

japan <- maplibre(style = carto_style("positron"), center = c(135, 35), zoom = 4) |>
  add_fill_layer(
    id = "prefectures",
    source = jp_prefectures,
    fill_color = interpolate(
      column = "aged_65",
      values = c(22, 30, 40),
      stops = c("#fee8c8", "#fdbb84", "#b30000")
    ),
    fill_opacity = 0.85
  )

What am I looking at? add_view_summary()

A panel that summarises the features in view and compares them with the whole map.

japan |>
  add_view_summary(
    layer_id = "prefectures",
    column = "aged_65",
    label = "Aged 65 and over",
    name_column = "prefecture",
    weight = "pop_2024",
    weight_label = "population",
    unit = "prefectures",
    suffix = "%"
  )

Options:

  • stat: "mean" (the default), "median" or "sum". "sum" suits absolute values, such as population, and shows the share of the total in view: “16.8M, 36% of total”. Values of a million or more are abbreviated.
  • weight: a column to weight the mean or median, such as population.
  • compact = TRUE: only the count, the value and the comparison.
  • collapsed: the button in the corner collapses the panel to its title and value. On maps narrower than 480 px, such as on phones, the panel starts collapsed; collapsed = FALSE keeps it open and collapsible = FALSE removes the button.
  • color: one color for the histogram instead of the map’s colors.

Which ones stand out here? add_view_ranking()

A live list of the features in view with the highest values, or the lowest with order = "asc". Each entry shows a bar on the scale of the whole map and its overall rank (#2 = second of all). Click on a name to go there.

japan |>
  add_view_ranking(
    layer_id = "prefectures",
    column = "change",
    name_column = "prefecture",
    label = "Population change 2020-2024",
    order = "asc",
    unit = "prefectures",
    suffix = "%"
  )

Is this value high or low? add_context_tooltip()

A tooltip that shows a feature’s value together with its rank, the share of features below it, its difference with the average, and a small strip of the whole distribution with the feature marked. Use it instead of the layer’s own tooltip, or both will show.

japan |>
  add_context_tooltip(
    layer_id = "prefectures",
    column = "aged_65",
    name_column = "prefecture",
    label = "Aged 65 and over",
    weight = "pop_2024",
    unit = "prefectures",
    suffix = "%"
  )

Where is this place? add_feature_search()

A search box over a column of your data. Matching ignores case and accents (“tokyo” finds “Tokyo”, “cordoba” finds “Córdoba”), and detail_column tells apart repeated names. Choosing a result moves the map there and outlines it. It works with the keyboard: arrows, Enter and Escape.

Unlike mapgl::add_geocoder_control(), which searches places around the world, this searches the map’s own data.

japan |>
  add_feature_search(layer_id = "prefectures", search_column = "prefecture")

Point layers

All the components work with point layers too (add_circle_layer(), add_symbol_layer()), clustered or not. On a clustered layer every point in view counts, whether it is drawn on its own or inside a cluster.

Earthquakes get deeper from west to east, following the Nazca plate as it sinks under South America. Zoom from the Chilean coast to Santiago del Estero and the average depth goes from about 56 km to about 200 km:

maplibre(style = carto_style("positron"), center = c(-66, -33), zoom = 4) |>
  add_circle_layer(
    id = "earthquakes",
    source = earthquakes,
    circle_color = interpolate(
      column = "depth",
      values = c(0, 100, 300, 600),
      stops = c("#fde725", "#21918c", "#3b528b", "#440154")
    ),
    circle_radius = 4,
    circle_stroke_color = "white",
    circle_stroke_width = 0.5
  ) |>
  add_view_summary(
    layer_id = "earthquakes",
    column = "depth",
    label = "Depth",
    name_column = "place",
    unit = "earthquakes",
    digits = 0,
    suffix = " km",
    labels = context_labels(highest = "Deepest", lowest = "Shallowest")
  )
